summary: No injection, secret or trust-boundary defect in the post-PR feedback diff; three non-blocking resource and error-handling defects remain, the most relevant being unbounded growth of outcomes and evidence links driven by review volume.

findings.summary: Each CHANGES_REQUESTED review adds one stored outcome and one backlog evidence link with no cap, and every review page is read into memory with no output bound, so a review flood grows the outcome file and the feedback entry without limit.
findings.evidence: ENG-24 and ENG-21. feedback.py:75-89 (_review_outcomes) emits one outcome per review id with no cap; feedback.py:333 (_store) does body['outcomes'].extend(new) and rewrites the whole file each refresh; improvements.py:243 (add_feedback) does body['evidence'].append(link) with no length check, while the changes-requested key is per reviewer login, so distinct review ids from one login all accumulate on one entry. feedback.py:26-31 (run_gh) uses subprocess.run(capture_output=True) with no size bound, and feedback.py:184-197 reads all pages via gh api --paginate. Probe: one archived run with 300 CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews from one login produced an outcome file with 300 outcomes and a feedback entry with 300 evidence links in a single refresh. The 60 s timeout bounds time, not size.
findings.fix: Cap stored evidence links per feedback entry (for example the most recent N, with a count of omitted links) and cap or summarise outcomes per run; bound the gh output read (or stream and stop after a page limit) and report an overflow as a classified gap rather than storing it unbounded.

findings.summary: The outcome-file path is built by joining the unvalidated run branch into a single file name, so a branch containing '/' makes refresh fail for that run with an inaccessible gap on every refresh.
findings.evidence: ENG-25 (validate input reaching the file system). feedback.py:228-229 builds Path(home)/'outcomes'/improvements.backlog_name(repo, branch), and improvements.py:38-47 (_entry_name) embeds the same branch in feedback entry names. Git refname rules forbid '..' and leading dots, so this is not a traversal today, but '/' is legal in branch names. Probe with branch 'feature/slash-branch' returned refreshed=0 and gap class 'inaccessible' ('No such file or directory' for .../improvements/proj-feature/slash-branch.<hash>.feedback....json.<pid>.tmp); the same run with a plain branch refreshed cleanly. The gap is reported, not silent, but the run is never recorded.
findings.fix: Derive the file-name component from a slug or hash of the branch (keeping the real branch in the body and in run matching), or reject separators up front as a classified 'missing' gap; apply the same change to the retro entry name, which shares _entry_name.

findings.summary: An OS error while creating the outcomes lock escapes refresh as a traceback instead of becoming a classified gap, so the whole command aborts and other archived runs are not refreshed.
findings.evidence: ENG-17 and FR-012 (other runs still refresh; an OS problem is classified inaccessible or transient). feedback.py:320-322 catches only lock.LockHeld around _acquire_home_lock(directory, 'feedback'); lock.acquire can raise PermissionError from os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL). _store() does not catch it and refresh() (feedback.py:358-373) catches only Gap, and cmd_feedback catches only ValueError. Probe: home directory made read-only with two archived runs; refresh raised PermissionError on outcomes.lock.json and returned no report, so run 'run-b' was never attempted. No data was corrupted, since the lock was never taken.
findings.fix: Catch OSError alongside lock.LockHeld in _store's lock acquisition and convert it to a Gap (class 'inaccessible'), so the failing run is reported and the remaining runs still refresh.
